reflexion_entries_to_archive.text: S139 P1: S138 shipped damageEntity as 'the ONE way anything in the world takes damage' - typed, serialized, hashed, 22 passing tests, a docblock stating the contract, and a handoff recording the blocker as GONE. A.0 found it had ZERO production call sites. The only importer in the entire repo was its own test file, while three live damage paths went on calling damageCreature directly. It was correct, tested, dead code for a full session. The reason no test caught it is the important part: all 22 unit tests called damageEntity THEMSELVES, so every one passed while the game never invoked it once. The defect was not in the function's behaviour, it was the ABSENCE OF AN EDGE from the game to the function - a property of the import graph, which no behavioural test can see. Two durable lessons. (a) 'Shipped' means called, not merely present and green; a new dispatcher's acceptance criterion must include a named production caller. (b) When a claim is about reachability, the guard has to read the import graph - damage.wired.test.ts is a filesystem scan for exactly that reason, and it strips comments first so a docblock mentioning the symbol cannot masquerade as a call site.

S139 P1: the obvious lock test was PRIMITIVE_MAX_HP === 1000. That would have been nearly worthless. The number is not load-bearing as a number - it is load-bearing because 1%, 2.5% and 5% of it are INTEGERS, which is what makes damageEntity's integer guard unfireable at runtime. Pinning the value still permits someone to 'improve' it to 1024 and silently destroy that property. So the tests assert the RELATIONSHIPS: the percentages land on integers, DOT_CADENCE_TICKS === 0.5*PHYSICS_HZ, and attackFireTick === chewHits * CHEW_INTERVAL_TICKS for every chewing config. That last one existed ONLY as a comment ('chewHits: 5, // = constants.ts CHEW_HITS') beside two hardcoded literals, and A.0b measured that breaking it makes the sever dispatch never fire - the chew caps forever with the bond intact. Generalisation: when you lock a constant, first ask what PROPERTY makes it correct, and lock that. Also add a non-vacuity assertion (chewers.length > 0), or a future refactor that empties the collection turns the guard green and silent.

S139 P2: I fixed two spawn bugs that A.0b had FOUND FOR ME, then wrote a goblin that closed on its target, entered ATTACKING, and never hit anything. Every unit test passed. The FSM state was right, the target was right, the range test was right - and the damage never landed, because the Voltkin ATTACKING bounce aborts when `!bondValid && !creatureValid` and both are false for a structure attacker, so it bounced out before its fire tick on every single cycle. What caught it was the real-physics acceptance test asserting the VICTIM'S HP ACTUALLY DECREASED. A state assertion (is it ATTACKING? does it have a target?) would have passed happily. What made it diagnosable in two minutes was a throwaway scratch test that printed state/ticksInState/distance/hp every 80 ticks: `tis 0` recurring at ticks 160/240/320 with hp pinned at 1000 named the mechanism immediately. Two lessons. (a) The acceptance criterion for a new attacker is that the TARGET changed, never that the attacker reached a state. (b) This is the same defect class as P1's dead dispatcher - correct code that is never actually reached - and I reproduced it in the very session I spent fixing it. Assume you will too, and write the test that observes the EFFECT.

S139 P4: e2e/smoke.spec.ts asserted 'v15' while PROTOCOL_VERSION was 17, and set a peer override of 16 for a test titled 'Newer-version joiner' - so a test whose entire purpose was the newer-peer branch had silently inverted into the older-peer branch. S133 P2 had ALREADY FIXED this exact defect once, and left a ⛔ comment saying a future bump must update this line and the two below. It recurred anyway, and stayed invisible because the describe is @quarantine-flaky and the gating lane grep-inverts that tag, so nothing could go red. The lesson is not 'read the warning'. A comment asking a human to keep three numbers in sync across one file is not an invariant, it is a wish; and the second recurrence is the evidence. The fix is structural: ONE `LOCAL_PROTO_V` with `NEWER_PEER_V = LOCAL_PROTO_V + 1` DERIVED, so the inversion cannot be expressed. When you find a stale constant that a prior session already fixed once, do not fix the value - delete the opportunity.
